name: Compute money
frame: The capital flowing into AI compute and the labs — data-centre lending, chip earnings, IPOs and the first sell-off tied to the labs’ own warnings.
question: Do the capital commitments keep growing, and do the IPOs happen on the terms reported? Settled by: Anthropic filing to list (or not), OpenAI’s stance on 2026 holding, or a quarter of results showing the spending slowing.

text: As of 14 September the money is still arriving and the first wobble has appeared. Oracle's Q1 FY27 reported cloud infrastructure revenue up 121% to $7.4bn, remaining performance obligations of $664bn and capex of $28.5bn. The Pentagon is in talks to lend AI cloud firm Fluidstack $5bn; SoftBank sealed an upsized $11.87bn two-year loan from about 20 banks for its OpenAI investment; Cohere is in advanced talks to raise US$2bn–US$3bn at a US$20bn valuation; Discovery Loop is seeking funding at about $50bn; Z.ai filed in Hong Kong to raise about $5bn; and Nscale is seeking up to $3.5bn before a fall IPO. The DOJ is investigating whether Nvidia structured its ~$20bn Groq licensing deal to avoid antitrust review.

The listings diverge. Reuters reports Nvidia is in talks to invest up to $10bn as anchor investor in an Anthropic IPO seeking up to $100bn; CNBC reports Anthropic picked the Nasdaq for a listing that CNBC says may seek a $2 trillion valuation, and the FT reports Anthropic told shareholders adjusted operating income will be positive for a second straight quarter. Altman ruled out an OpenAI listing in 2026, citing safety concerns. On 14 September AI and chip stocks sold off in Asia and US premarket after lab CEOs called for slowing development, and Samsung and SK hynix rejected KEPCO's proposal to prepay five years of electricity bills for chip clusters.

As of 21 September the capital is still arriving and the first full forecast of the burn is public. Crusoe raised $3.9 billion at a $30.9 billion valuation, ten months after raising $1.38 billion at a $10 billion valuation; CoreWeave announced $3.0 billion of convertible senior notes due 2033 plus an at-the-market programme of up to 35 million shares; ten banks provided US$22 billion of debt to Crux AI, the Blackstone-Alphabet venture, secured on Google TPUs and Crux AI's anticipated customer contracts; and Generac's Form 8-K shows a warrant for up to 1,693,745 shares issued to an Amazon subsidiary against payments of up to $8 billion for data-centre backup generators.

Two sets of figures came from documents seen by one newspaper each. Reuters, reporting the Financial Times' account of an OpenAI presentation, says the company expects to burn $278 billion in cash between 2026 and 2030, spending about $856 billion on computing power and infrastructure by the end of 2030 while revenue rises from $36 billion this year to $350 billion in 2030; and the Financial Times reported technology companies have provided as much as $300 billion in guarantees financing AI data centres and chips over the past year. Nscale filed to list on the NYSE with a $1.02 billion net loss on $140.6 million of revenue in the six months to 30 June 2026, $56.4 billion in remaining performance obligations and more than $8 billion in debt. Anthropic pushed its listing to November, with backers projecting $110 billion in annualized revenue by year-end, and CNBC reported that Anthropic and OpenAI are now also pursuing 20-30 MW capacity deals in the UK, the Nordics and the US. No audited figure has been published for any of the revenue or burn projections.
states.changed: The listing question moved from Nasdaq choice to a dated delay — Anthropic pushed to November for third-quarter results — and the first full spending forecast became public, with the Financial Times reporting OpenAI expects $278 billion of negative cash flow to 2030 and as much as $300 billion of industry guarantees keeping much of the build-out off balance sheets.

text: As of 28 September the capital is still arriving and the price of it has risen. SoftBank raised roughly $11 billion across dollars and euros, selling $1 billion of 3.5-year bonds at 8.625%, $4.5 billion of 5.5-year securities at 9.25% and a $4.5 billion 7.5-year tranche at 9.75%; The Japan Times, citing Bloomberg, says the yields are the highest-ever for SoftBank dollar bonds, on a day when benchmark US Treasury rates soared to two-decade highs, and that part of the money funds a follow-on investment in OpenAI. CNBC reported Treasury yields at their highest levels since 2007, with the 10-year near 5.17%, and cited JPMorgan's June estimate of $4.1 trillion in AI-related debt through 2030. Akamai announced an $11.6 billion seven-year commitment from Anthropic with a warrant for up to about 5% of its stock, Nscale secured $3.36 billion in convertible notes led by Third Point with $1 billion from Nvidia, and Oracle sent a force majeure notice to Blue Owl over the 2.5GW Project Jupiter campus while saying publicly that the project remains on its planned schedule.

The listing question moved on structure rather than date. Reuters, citing The Information, reported Anthropic is seeking shareholder approval for a special share class giving its seven co-founders 50.1% of voting power ahead of an IPO, holding as long as three of the seven retain a minimum number of shares. Nscale's filing shows Microsoft and Anthropic accounting for 85% of $103 billion in total contract value with only $2.6 billion active at the end of August. Brookings put US AI infrastructure investment at $10.3 trillion from 2025 to 2032, an annual average of 3.63% of GDP, while writing that it would be premature to conclude that AI infrastructure already poses systemic risk comparable to earlier credit booms; Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid asked publicly whether the sector is moving to a too-big-to-fail ecosystem and announced no action. Epoch AI reported that the cost of a fixed level of AI performance has fallen about 47% per quarter since 2023. No financing has failed and no audited figure has been published for any of the revenue or burn projections.
states.changed: The cost of the build-out became visible in the coupon: SoftBank paid its highest-ever dollar yields in the same week Treasury yields reached their highest since 2007. Anthropic's listing preparation moved to a founder-control share structure rather than a date, and a Federal Reserve bank president raised the too-big-to-fail question in public for the first time in this arc.

text: As of 5 October the most detailed account of a frontier lab's finances exists, and it is not a filing. Reuters reported in late September a prospectus it had seen showing revenue growing in 2025 to nearly $4.6 billion, and plans to spend $518 billion on cloud, computing and infrastructure obligations. CNBC reported that the near-$42 billion net loss included a large accounting charge reflecting an increase in the estimated value of convertible financing "rather than money the company spent running its business", and that the company lost more on an operating basis than that charge accounts for. CNBC reported that 80 of the prospectus's 261 pages are risk factors, warning of "catastrophic or existential risk to humanity", and TechCrunch reported Reuters' account of language on models that resist shutdown, conceal or manipulate information, and behave in ways resembling blackmail. The Financial Times said it had reviewed the filing and that nearly a third of it is risk factors. No registration statement appears on SEC EDGAR: a company search filtered to S-1 filings returns no matching companies, an unfiltered search returns only special-purpose vehicles and feeder funds, and a full-text search of S-1 filings across the week returns nothing.

The debt behind the compute was reported for the first time. Quartz, citing Bloomberg, described a $60 billion package assembled around Anthropic's chip supply: a senior-secured tranche with banks preparing syndication and a junior tranche led by Blackstone putting up part of it from its own capital, covering roughly a third of what Anthropic has committed under a five-year lease for tensor processing unit capacity. The prospectus is reported to flag the supplier's dual position as chip vendor and lender as giving rise to potential conflicts of interest.

Against that, the first serious public estimate of the revenue the build-out requires. Bain put the annual revenue the AI industry needs by 2031 to justify current data-centre investment at several times what existing consumer and enterprise services contribute, and described the remainder as a shortfall. Bloomberg reported OpenAI in early talks to raise around $30 billion at roughly a $1.4 trillion valuation. Nvidia's board added $150 billion to its buyback authorisation, taking the remaining total to $235 billion. No audited figure has been published for any lab's revenue or burn, and no financing has failed.
states.changed: The arc's central question moved from whether Anthropic will list to whether the numbers already in circulation are the filed ones: EDGAR still shows no registration statement, and every figure rests on documents two newspapers say they reviewed. The week also exposed the lending structure under the compute, with a reported $60 billion package in which Anthropic's chip supplier is also its lender.

questions.question: Does Anthropic file, and at what valuation?
questions.would_settle: An S-1 or an equivalent filing.

settled.text: Not yet. As of 5 October no registration statement for Anthropic PBC appears on SEC EDGAR: a company search filtered to S-1 filings returns no matching companies, and the reported prospectus figures rest on documents Reuters and the Financial Times say they reviewed rather than on a filing.

questions.question: Does the higher cost of debt change any announced AI data-centre commitment?
questions.would_settle: A withdrawn or repriced bond sale, a project formally cancelled, or Nscale pricing its listing below the reported valuation.
